answer: Tie each agent identity to a costly, non-transferable history: to earn spending rights, an agent must stake tokens, slashed for duplicate behavior, and build reputation over many epochs of verified work. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted status costs weeks of compute and locked capital, and cloning thousands of identities means paying that price for every copy. An abandoned identity is a relic, not a shortcut, as reputation decays without honest work. Like a meadow yielding only after seasons of tending, trust grows slowly, is costly to fake at scale, and cheap to verify.
